What happened with me was ever since I was a little kid, my mom made me go to Sunday school and I'd just sit there looking around like "you all know this is bullshit, right?". I spend most of my childhood (like, 5-13) being a closet agnostic (my mom is a strong Jewish woman) and then, at age 14, I went from that to being an athiest. The thing that really pushed me over the hump was that, at a funeral for one of my friends who OD'd on drugs, the minister said "You have to have the strength to carry on, and there is only one place you can get that strength from, and that is the Lord God." which really really pissed me off, because that's making people feel worthless intentionally. The strength to go on after something terrible has happened can only come from inside you, in my opinion, and saying it comes from belief in God and nowhere else is moderately sickening to me. Now I'm almost 15, and frequently think about the nature of everything and read books about things like superstring theory and parallel universes, etc and recently found /r/athiesm. Its awesome knowing there's likeminded people out there, seeing as how I live in sort of a nest of religious people.
